blocks.text: Deuteronomy 20 contains 20 verses. It opens with: When thou goest forth to battle against thine enemies, and seest horses, and chariots, `and' a people more than thou, thou shalt not be afraid of them; for Jehovah thy God is with thee, who brought thee up out of the land of Egypt. It concludes with: Only the trees of which thou knowest that they are not trees for food, thou shalt destroy and cut them down; and thou shalt build bulwarks against the city that maketh war with thee, until it fall. Supplied contextual evidence for this passage adds: The herem and warfare commands require historical, literary, ethical, and canonical examination and must not be generalized into permission for modern religious violence.
